A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JDR research and contain the complete 40-page paper, including Appendices A.1–A.9. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic and real-world node-classification experiments in Section 3, plus runtime measurements, ablations, clustering experiments, and simulations in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 3 and the appendices, including benchmark performance, runtime measurements, ablations, and simulations.

M1.justification: JDR's spectral decomposition, interpolation, graph and feature synthesis, iteration, and sparsification procedures are unchanged in Section 2.3 and Algorithm 1. The mathematical corrections do not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same cSBM scenarios and real-world graph datasets, including the additional heterophilic benchmarks, larger graphs, and spectral-clustering evaluations in the appendices.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the experiments, including DIGL, FoSR, BORF, AMP-BP, and MLP. Describing AMP-BP as an 'optimal algorithm' instead of an 'optimal baseline' does not change its participation or role.

E3.justification: The sparse and dense splits, benchmark-specific splits, metrics, model configurations, hyperparameter searches, and appendix experimental procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same graph-only versus feature-only ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, alignment and ESNR analyses, DIGL combination experiments, and supplementary simulations in Appendices A.5, A.6, and A.9.

E5.justification: Both report 100 random-split runs for general experiments and 95% confidence intervals using 1,000 bootstrap samples. Appendix A.9 also retains its ten independent trials and standard-deviation reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including the main benchmark tables, appendix runtime and supplementary results, ablation curves, and simulation outcomes. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Limited formal corrections resolve inconsistent variable binding: Proposition 1 replaces eta_B and its bound with eta_X, matching the feature perturbation, and Appendix A.3 changes the summation index defining z from i to j to match its summand. It also corrects 'eigenvalue' to 'eigenvector' and removes an unused E shorthand equality. The intended guarantee and proof strategy remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint spectral alignment, improved downstream node classification, theoretical justification under a stylized model, and performance against existing rewiring methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including dependence on node features, restriction to node classification, scalability caveats, cSBM linearity assumptions, and the Minesweeper failure discussion.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, hyperparameter tables, hardware and runtime disclosures, processing instructions, and code-access information are unchanged in the main text and appendices.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to rewiring, denoising, graph structure learning, and regularization remain unchanged. The AMP-BP wording edit does not alter its relationship to JDR.

P1.justification: There are a few localized wording and terminology corrections, including singular 'eigenvector' and the AMP-BP description, together with notation cleanup and the updated version stamp. Section ordering and the narrative structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their content, captions, and placement. The proof has minor equation typography and spacing adjustments, including removal of the redundant E equality line, with limited local text reflow.

improvement.justification: v4 improves mathematical clarity and internal consistency by correcting the parameter bounds in Proposition 1 and the summation index and terminology in Appendix A.3. Removing unused shorthand also simplifies the proof's presentation. These are limited benefits; the method, empirical support, substantive theoretical guarantee, and conclusions remain unchanged.
